summary: Added MeetsGrader, delegating to evals/rebuilt/domain.py's Outcome.meets() -- the already-correct, already-tested eleven-vocabulary grading logic (go/no_go/speak/silence/reply/no_reply/create/update/none/either/remind, plus a judge's verdict and the corpus's own structural checks) -- instead of reimplementing a subset of it in a new grader, ahead of porting the 150 existing corpus cases onto the S1-S9 scenario map.
details: AbsenceGrader covers only silence/speak/go/no_go and is left unchanged (already shipped and tested for S4-S7's hand-written cases). MeetsGrader is the port's grader: several corpora (proactive_decide/proactive_act -> S1, note_candidates -> S6, being_contradicted/identity_grounding/source_scope -> S3) need create/update/remind/either/a judge's FAIL-or-REVIEW verdict, which AbsenceGrader was never built to read.

New environment_state signals NORA_CHANGED/NORA_JUDGED/NORA_CHECKS_FAILED carry Outcome.changed/.judged/.checks_failed through evals.backbone._drive(), alongside the existing NORA_ADMITTED/NORA_SAID/NORA_WRITTEN. MeetsGrader reconstructs a real Outcome from these seven signals and calls .meets(expect) directly, so a future change to that method (or its own test suite) covers this grader for free rather than needing to be re-derived a second time.

Also extended Spec/_drive() to read a per-case room/now/policy/config from Case.metadata, falling through to Spec's own experiment-wide defaults when absent -- the existing corpora (proactive_decide.yaml in particular) name a real room and a real now PER CASE, which one Spec shared across a whole Experiment batch could not express.
Falsified: hardcoding MeetsGrader's verdict to True turned all 7 of its new tests red before the real delegation was restored. 44 tests in test_eval_backbone.py, full suite 7944 passed.
